messages:
maria: Customer reported duplicate external actions (two charges, two emails) after we returned what looked like a transient error.
maria: Short repro from them: they call our /v1/chat endpoint with function_call to `charge_card`, the client times out after 6s, retries the same request. The logs show two function executions with different request-ids but same payload.
ajay: do we have the raw payload + response headers? specifically `x-request-id` and status codes
maria: pasted sanitized request & timeline below:
```
POST /v1/chat
Body: {"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"charge $200"}], "function_call": {"name":"charge_card","arguments":{"amount":200}} }
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
```
maria: server logs:
- 202  x-request-id=rx-01A23 (accepted to async queue)
- then client retried after client timeout => second request
- second request processed, 200 x-request-id=rx-01A24
maria: customer says they never got a 202, their client timed out waiting for response and retried. our system processed both.
ajay: hm. did the function executor actually run twice or did one run and the other short-circuit via de-dup?
dan: I pulled the executor logs — two distinct execs for charge_card with matching args, different exec-ids. It called our payment webhook both times. No de-dup at executor layer.
kelsey: billing: customer hit two charges. We refunded one already but need root cause and mitigation.
ajay: possible contributing factor: our async path returns 202 when work enqueued. If client doesn't propagate an idempotency key, retry will cause duplicate work. But also check if model fallback retried the function call due to schema validation error — that can cause duplicate invocation from the model side.
maria: there is one suspicious line earlier: function executor returned a malformed result that failed our schema checker, so we logged a schema validation error and the conversation re-issued `function_call` in a follow-up message. So timeline shows: first exec returned malformed JSON -> model issued another `function_call` -> client retried due to timeout -> => three signals but two actual webhook hits.
ajay: ok that explains hybrid duplicate: both client retries and model re-call. We should treat these as independent duplication vectors.
dan: repro steps I ran locally:
1) send request without idempotency header
2) simulate executor returning `{"status": "ok"` (missing closing brace) for first call
3) client triggers a retry (simulate 6s timeout)
Result: executor invoked twice
maria: thanks. Customer asked for short-term mitigation they can do now.
kelsey: immediate customer guidance: add an idempotency token header on client side (Idempotency-Key) OR make payment webhooks idempotent on their side (dedupe by charge metadata). We refunded and paused the customer's live webhook for 2 hours.
ajay: longer-term: infra fixes:
- require idempotency-key header for any function that triggers billing/external side-effects (configurable per function)
- executor: persist execution fingerprint and reject replays within 24h (return 409 with existing exec-id)
- runtime: avoid returning 202 for sync-intended flows; if we accept async, ensure we surface exec-id so clients can query status rather than retrying blindly
- improve schema validation: if executor returns invalid schema, mark the function as failed (do NOT allow model to re-call automatically without guard), and surface human-visible error to customer instead of a quiet follow-up call
maria: can we add a quick patch to the executor to dedupe by request payload hash + customer id? even as a short-term toggle?
dan: yes I can add a toggle. I'll ship a small in-memory cache keyed by (customer-id, function-name, payload-hash) with 1h TTL behind a feature flag. Will instrument stats.
akay: sorry meant ajay :thinking_face:
ajay: assign to eng-runtime and mark P1 for now. Create ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-9642
maria: noted. Support ticket 54321 assigned, customer notified about refund and recommended idempotency header.
kelsey: billing will follow-up with formal refund confirmation and billing adjustment.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026, owners: @dan, @ajay, due in 4h
maria: for reproduction I'll attach the curl we used to simulate timeouts and the broken executor response. keeping the thread updated.
ajay: follow-ups: (1) dan to ship dedupe toggle (2) runtime to add exec-id in 202 response (3) docs + SDK: add example for Idempotency-Key on function calls
maria: thanks team :thumbsup:
